title: Free AI diagram maker: flowcharts, mind maps, timelines · {name}
description: Describe a process or drop a report in a browser tab, and get a flowchart, a mind map, a timeline or a page to play with. Free, nothing to install.
h1: AI that answers with a diagram, not a wall of text.
lede: Ask {name} in your own words, or drop a report in. A process comes back as a flowchart, ideas as a mind map, a plan as a timeline, a sum as a page you can play with, all drawn right in the answer, in your language. Nothing to install.

where.title: Where your words go.
where.why: There is no {name} server. What changes is the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: Your files and your tasks are kept in this browser, encrypted. Nothing reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and the file’s text go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
With the AI on this computer, nothing leaves it. It needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers.
A diagram shows what the AI understood. Read it as you would a colleague’s sketch before you send it on.
The AI writes a page’s formulas: try one with an answer you already know.
An AI on this computer gets pages like these right less often than a large one online, and may answer in words.
A map’s background comes from a map service, once you’ve said yes. The AI places the stops, and can get one wrong.
Diagrams aren’t pictures. For an illustration, ask for a picture, which takes an AI that draws them.
Your work lives in this browser. Clear its data without a backup and it’s gone.
faq.items: Is it free, with no sign-up?
Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Can it make a mind map from a PDF?
Yes. Drop the PDF in the box and ask. A scanned PDF, with no text in it, isn’t read.
Can I change a diagram by hand?
There’s no drawing board: ask for the change in your own words, and it’s drawn again. To work on it elsewhere, Copy gives you its text, in Mermaid, a format many editors read.
How do I get it into my slides or my report?
Its Copy button puts it on the clipboard as a picture: paste it into your document or your slide.
Does it work in my language?
Yes. Its words are in the language you write in, and numbers are written as your language writes them.
Does it work on a phone?
In the browser, yes. The AI on this computer needs a computer; on a phone, choose one online.
